Operator: Welcome to The Clorox Company Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Today's call is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the call over to Lisah Burhan, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Linda Rendle: Good afternoon, and thank you for joining us. Today, we reported Q2 net sales decrease of 16% to $1.45 billion, impacted by the August cyberattack. Gross margin expanded 200 bps to 38.4%, driven by cost savings and pricing. For the full year, we expect net sales to be down mid-single digits, and adjusted EPS between $4.30 and $4.50. We remain cautious given macroeconomic headwinds and consumer spending pressure.

Kevin Grundy: Thanks, good afternoon. Can you talk about consumer elasticities and market share recovery following the cyberattack? Are you expecting promotional spending to increase in the back half?

Linda Rendle: What I would say is that it is too early to tell regarding long-term elasticity trends. We continue to monitor consumer behavior closely. We are focused on executing our strategic initiatives and driving long-term shareholder value.

Operator: Welcome to Apple's Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Today's call is being recorded.

Tim Cook: Good afternoon. Apple is reporting revenue of $90.8 billion for the March quarter. Services reached an all-time revenue record of $23.9 billion. We expect revenue to grow low-single digits next quarter, though we remain cautious on macroeconomic conditions.

Tami Zakaria: Could you provide more color on China demand and whether gross margins will sustain at 46%?

Luca Maestri: We believe gross margins will remain between 45.5% and 46.5%. As you know, the important thing is we continue to focus on operational excellence.

Operator: Welcome to Microsoft's Fiscal Year 2024 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call.

Satya Nadella: Welcome everyone. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $35.1 billion, up 23% year-over-year. We continue to see strong demand across our commercial offerings.

Brent Thill: Can you give us an update on Azure AI contribution and capital expenditures for the upcoming quarters?

Amy Hood: Capital expenditures were $14 billion in Q3, and we expect capex to increase sequentially to support cloud demand. However, we remain cautious regarding hardware supply constraints.
